key_idea: Reduce the height-zero characterization of abelian defect groups to quasi-simple groups, then prove a classification-wide statement that non-cyclic blocks have characters in at least three Aut(S)-orbits (or constant degree), so that automorphisms acting on the defect group would break the all-height-zero condition.
reason: The argument is a large reduction-and-classification proof. It relies on CFSG-based case analysis across sporadic, alternating, and Lie-type groups, uses GAP character-table checks, and adds many special patches such as E6 at p=3 and the type A/D4/D5 subcases, so a global reason is hard to see. The orbit-counting idea in Theorem 15 is a sensible organizing principle, but it is buried under heavy bookkeeping and Lusztig-series and Bonnafé–Rouquier technicalities.
recognized: Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture, the 'if' direction for odd p: Malle–Navarro–Schaeffer Fry–Tiep, 'Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture' (Annals), building on reductions by Navarro–Späth and Ruhstorfer
